body:
Jonas Weber: Hey folks — prompt sets gap analysis is ready, and we need help pulling in real-world prompts from teams before we lock pilot coverage. Doc here (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rwi-redwood-guardrails-prompts (see “prompt-set-gap-analysis”).

Jonas Weber: TL;DR gaps we need to close for Optimize guardrails gating:
- Tool-calling / function args correctness (esp retries + partial failures)
- Structured output (JSON schema adherence + “no extra keys”)
- Long-context summarization w/ retrieval snippets (8–32k) + hallucination sensitivity
- Customer support style chats (tone + policy compliance)
- Fintech-ish: transaction dispute + audit-style responses (high factuality bar)
- Multilingual (ES/DE) + code-switching

Jonas Weber: Ask: if you own/know a workload in any of these buckets, can you contribute ~10–25 prompts + expected success criteria? Doesn’t need gold answers for all, but we need at least pass/fail rubric or key checks.

Jonas Weber: Requirements:
- NO customer PII. Please anonymize (NAME_1, COMPANY_1, etc) and remove IDs/tickets.
- Include prompt + relevant system/tool spec + any constraints (“must be valid JSON”, “cite sources”, etc)
- Add tags: `workload`, `surface` (chat/tool/structured), `risk` (formatting/factuality/toxicity), `avg_ctx_len`.

Jonas Weber: Template + instructions are in the folder too (“prompt-contribution-template”). If you’d rather paste into a doc, that’s fine — we’ll convert.

Selene Huang: :eyes: thanks Jonas. Are we assuming these get used for gating only, or also for the nightly sentinel suite?

Jonas Weber: Both ideally. We’ll label which ones are “gating suites” vs “sentinel” (lightweight). Sentinel needs to be stable + cheap; gating can be heavier.

Sana Farid: For “expected success criteria” — do you want numeric rubrics (1-5) or binary checks? Some teams won’t have graders.

Jonas Weber: Whatever you have. If you can do binary checks, that’s ok (e.g., “valid JSON”, “contains all required fields”, “tool args parse”). For qualitative tasks, a 1–5 rubric + short guidance helps. We can also run rubric LLM-judge for now but want human-grounded definitions.

Karthik Iyer: +1. Also would be good to note if prompts are sensitive to temperature / sampling. Some regressions we saw are basically “reasoning depth” vs formatting.

Jonas Weber: Yep — add optional fields: `sampling_sensitivity` (low/med/high) and `must_not` constraints (e.g., “don’t mention internal policy”).

Olivia Grant: Question from eval-harness side: preferred format? JSONL? YAML? If we can standardize now it’ll save pain when we ingest.

Jonas Weber: Today: template is YAML per prompt (easiest for humans). We’ll convert to JSONL for harness ingestion. If you’re already sitting on JSONL, drop it in.

Logan Wright: + note: please don’t include any real tenant names in tags. We’ll be exporting aggregated stats and cardinality can get gnarly.

Jonas Weber: Good call. Tags should be generic categories only. If you need to indicate “enterprise-like”, use `tier=enterprise_like` not company.

Diego Ramos: I can add a set of “post-change quality signals” prompts too? E.g., ones that tend to trigger user complaints (tone drift, refusal weirdness). Might help correlate gating failures w/ support cases.

Jonas Weber: Yes please. Those are super valuable. Add tag `source=support_signal` and we’ll keep them in the sentinel bucket initially.

Sofia Ivanova: From runtime: for batching/caching changes, we’ve seen output ordering issues and truncation edge cases. Should we include prompts that stress streaming + partial tool calls?

Jonas Weber: 100%. If you have minimal repro prompts that catch “streaming chunk boundary” weirdness or tool-call fragmentation, those are perfect guardrail prompts.

Wei Chen: For docs + future BYO prompt sets, do we want to enforce anonymization rules in the template? Like a checklist.

Jonas Weber: Yep — added a checklist section but happy for you to suggest stronger wording. We’ll probably add an automated scanner later, but for now we need contributors to self-certify.

Selene Huang: Timeline? When do you need contributions for pilot?

Jonas Weber: EOW next Friday would be amazing (so we can curate + de-dup). If you can’t hit that, still send — but pilot suite selection will start Monday.

Sana Farid: Are we weighting gaps by customer impact or by “regression likelihood”? Just asking because we’ll have limited evaluator budget.

Jonas Weber: For pilot: prioritize high customer impact + high likelihood of regression under Optimize changes (quantization + aggressive caching). The gap analysis doc has a “priority” column — feel free to disagree in comments.

Karthik Iyer: I’ll ping applied folks for multilingual + code-switching prompts. We have some internal ones but they’re a bit synthetic.

Jonas Weber: :thumbsup: thank you.

Olivia Grant: If anyone drops prompts in weird formats, tag me in the doc — I can help normalize.

Jonas Weber: Appreciate it. Also: please leave comments directly in “prompt-set-gap-analysis” if you think we’re missing an entire scenario class.

Logan Wright: One more: if you include tool-calling prompts, include the tool schema (names + required args). Otherwise we can’t run deterministically.

Jonas Weber: +1. Include tool schema inline or link in the same folder. Don’t link to private repos.

Selene Huang: Got it. I’ll contribute a set for structured output + “no extra keys” (this is where we saw formatting drift with quant).

Jonas Weber: Perfect — that’s exactly the gap we need to close. Thanks all.
